record.original_question: Let E be a Banach lattice and let C : E → E be a positive quasinilpotent compact operator. Do there exist positive operators, A, B : E → E such that C = AB − BA with one of A and B compact?

evidence.quote: Problem 17 (Positive commutator problem). Let E be a Banach lattice and let C : E → E be a positive quasinilpotent compact operator. Do there exist positive operators, A, B : E → E such that C = AB − BA with one of A and B compact?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $E$ be a Banach lattice, and let $C : E \to E$ be a positive, quasinilpotent, compact operator (positive means $C$ maps the positive cone of $E$ into itself; quasinilpotent means the spectral radius $r(C) = \lim_{n\to\infty}\|C^n\|^{1/n} = 0$). Do there exist positive operators $A, B : E \to E$ such that
$$C = AB - BA,$$
with at least one of $A$, $B$ compact?
artifact.status_search_result: The converse direction—that a positive commutator $AB-BA$ with $A,B$ positive and one compact is necessarily quasinilpotent—has been established (Drnovšek, Gao, and others). The existence question of whether every positive quasinilpotent compact operator arises as such a commutator does not appear to have a known solution in the literature; it is posed as an open problem in recent surveys.

status_evidence.title: Positive self-commutators of positive operators (arXiv:2501.03733)
status_evidence.snippet: A positive commutator of positive operators, provided one of them is compact, is necessarily quasinilpotent (Drnovšek, Gao).
status_evidence.claim: Only the necessity direction is known; the existence/representation question remains open.

status_evidence.title: More on positive commutators
status_evidence.snippet: Studies of when positive commutators AB-BA of positive operators are quasinilpotent, under compactness/Riesz assumptions.
status_evidence.claim: Literature addresses spectral properties of such commutators but not the inverse representation problem.
